rules.question: حال can be...
options: ...a مركب غير مفيد like: طالعَ جبلٍ
answer: ...a مركب غير مفيد like: طالعَ جبلٍ

rules.question: حال is always...
حال signifes upon...
options: ...the condition of the subject or object when the action is conducted.
...the method an action is conducted in.
...the place an action is conducted in.
...the reason for an action being conducted.
answer: ...the condition of the subject or object when the action is conducted.

rules.question: According to the Jamhoor, the حال will generally...
options: ...be in relation to the مضاف إليه.
...be in relation to the مفعول به.
...be in relation to the مفعول مطلق.
...be in relation to the مفعول فيه.
answer: ...be in relation to the مفعول به.
...be in relation to the مضاف إليه.

rules.question: The ذو الحال can be...
The ذو الحال...
The حال MUST precede the ذو الحال when...
options: ...the ذو الحال is جمع مؤنث سالم and منصوب.
...the ذو الحال is نكرة and منصوب.
answer: ...the ذو الحال is نكرة and منصوب.

rules.question: The حال...
If the حال is a مفزد, then it can be...
The حال and ذو الحال must correlate in...
If the ذو الحال is nonsensical plural, the حال...
options: ...will correlate in being plural and feminine or masculine depending on the gender of the nonsensical plural ذو الحال..

rules.question: If the حال is a جملة, then it must be a...
A رابط is brought in a حال when...
(continuing from Q13) In such a case...
A فعل مضارع حال can be preceded by...
A فعل مضارع must always contain a رابط...
An إسم جامد can not be a حال unless...
options: ...the اسم جامد has a مشتق نعت.
...the اسم جامد can be interpreted as a مشتق.
...the اسم جامد has a حال aswell.
answer: ...the اسم جامد can be interpreted as a مشتق.
...the اسم جامد has a مشتق نعت.

rules.question: The حال and the action preceding it...
options: ...should correspond in time but not always.
answer: ...should correspond in time but not always.

rules.question: When the حال is a فعل ماضي, generally, it has قد preceding it (provided there isn't a reason to prevent قد). The purpose of this قد is to...
options: ...provide a meaning of close past tense (القريب) in order to bring it close to the مضارع verb because the مضارع verb is the closest to an اسم الفاعل which is what حال should be in principle.
...provide a meaning of ceirtainty (التحقيق) in order to ascertain the حال so it is absolutely clear and ratified.
...provide a meaning of emphasis (التأكيد) in order to remove doubt since the حال is in the past and it could become doubtful.
answer: ...provide a meaning of close past tense (القريب) in order to bring it close to the مضارع verb because the مضارع verb is the closest to an اسم الفاعل which is what حال should be in principle.

rules.question: A فعل ماضي حال is prevented from being preceded by قد...
options: ...when the فعل ماضي comes after إلّا.
...when the فعل ماضي is free from a رابط.
...when the فعل ماضي is free from a واو حالية.
...when the فعل ماضي is connected with أو.
answer: ...when the فعل ماضي is connected with أو.
...when the فعل ماضي comes after إلّا.

rules.question: A فعل مضارع حال...
options: ...can never be preceded by قد, whether the واو حالية is there or not..
...can be preceded by قد only if the واو حالية is absent.
...can be preceded by قد and the واو حالية will also be necessary.
answer: ...can be preceded by قد and the واو حالية will also be necessary.

rules.question: A حال مقدرة is...
options: ...a حال which is in no tense (tenseless, timeless in another dimension) that's why it's called مقدّرة because it's to do with decree (تقدير).
...a حال which is in the past tense.
...a حال which is in the future tense.
...a حال which is in the present tense.
answer: ...a حال which is in the future tense.

parts.doubt: The explanation says the linking word (waw haaliyyah) is optional here because the present tense verb's object sits in front of it. No rule in the rules list says word order changes whether that linking word is optional. Every other example in this set with a plain positive present tense verb and no qad before it gets the linking word marked as not allowed at all, not optional (the birds turning away example, the two seas meeting example, the ones showing off while praying example). This mark breaks that pattern for a reason the rules never state. It could be right for a different reason, that the whole phrase seeds, he throws them to them, hangs together as one describing phrase rather than being its own separate haal sentence, but that reason is not in the rules either, so the mark cannot be confirmed from the rules alone.

parts.answer: All three are haal because that is "their" state when "they" receive the revelation. The first one does not take a waaw haaliyyah because it is a فعل ماضي which comes after الا. The second one requires a waaw haaliyyah because it is a jumla ismiyyah beginning with the dhameer raabit. The third one does not take waaw haaliyah because it is a mufrad haal and not a jumla.
parts.doubt: The middle line is marked as the linking word being necessary. The stated reason is that the sentence starts with the very pronoun that points back to the person in the state. No rule given says that starting with that pointing word forces the linking word to be there. A sibling example in this set (the one about the old man and his wife) has that same kind of pointing word inside its sentence, just not at the very start, and there the linking word is marked optional, not necessary. So the difference between necessary and optional seems to depend on where in the sentence the pointing word sits, but that distinction is not written in any rule here. The mark itself is not contradicted by anything, the reason just cannot be traced to a stated rule.

The first one doesn't take a waaw haaliyah because it's a فعل مضارغ منفي with a dhameer raabit. The second one is a jumlah ismiyyah which does not cotain a dhameer raabit, hence the waaw haaliyyah is necessary. The third one is also optional because it is a فعل ماضي with a dhameer raabit.
parts.doubt: This is the clearest problem found. The answer table marks the middle line, about the messenger calling you, as the linking word being optional. But the written explanation for that same line says the opposite, that the linking word is necessary, and gives as its reason that the sentence has no pointing word back to the listener. That reason looks wrong too, since the sentence does contain the word for calling you, and that you is the very same person the whole state is about, so a pointing word is present. Either the mark should say optional and the explanation is describing the wrong line, or the explanation is right and the mark should say necessary. As written, the explanation argues for a different answer than the one that was ticked.

parts.doubt: The explanation credits the optional linking word to the present tense verb carrying a pointing word back to the person in the state. But one of the rules given says a present tense verb must normally carry such a pointing word, except when it is preceded by the word lam, in which case that requirement is dropped entirely. So the real reason the linking word can be left out here is more likely the lam itself, not the pointing word the explanation names. The word in the sentence can plausibly still serve as a pointing word too, so the mark is probably fine, but the stated reason leans on something the rules do not clearly support instead of the lam exception the rules do state.

parts.question: Explain why you chose what you chose.
parts.answer: First one is haal because when "You" are arguing with me, the state "I" am in is that "Allah has guided me". And since the first one is فعل ماضي with a dhameer raabit, the "Yaa" in 'Hadanee', it is persimmable for it to have a waaw haaliyah. As for the second part, that also comes under the haaliyyah sentence. Since it is a فعل مضارع منفي with لا, it cannot take a waaw haaliyah, therefore the waaw before it is atifa making it معطوف to the haal before it. It is NOT an independent haal.

parts.answer: There should be a Waaw Haaliyyah before Qad because it is a فعل مضارع مثبت with قد and the dhameer raabit is present.

parts.question: Is the haal in this sentence, ثابتة, correctly used?
How many mistakes?
Explain the mistakes and how to rectify them.
parts.answer: The Zul Haal is the pronoun in the verb `راجع` which is in reference to Amir, who is a male, so the haal should correlate in number and gender. Therefore, it should be thaabitan (not thaabitatan)

examples.sentence: عَامِرٌ رَاجَعَ دُروسَه(ثابتة) بِلَا تُؤَدَةٍ فَرَسَب، لَاتكنْ مثلَ عامر

marked.style: small parenthetical annotation directly after دُروسَه

parts.question: Is the sentence إحترِمْ والِداكَ وَغَابَ أو حَضَرَا correct or incorrect in its grammar, including the haal clause وَغَابَ أو حَضَرَا?
How many mistakes?
Explain the mistakes and how to rectify them.
parts.answer: 1st, والداك should be والديك in the state of نصب because it's مفعول به of إحترم. 2nd, the waw haaliyah is not permissible because the construction of the haal is Fil Maadhi connected to 'Au' Harful ataf. 3rd, the verb غاب should be in the dual form غابا, because the Fa'il should be dual and in reference to 'والداك' both parents and therefore should correlate in number and gender.

examples.sentence: إحترِمْ والِداكَ وَغَابَ أو حَضَرَا

parts.question: Is the haal in this sentence, ثابتة, correctly used?
How many mistakes?
Explain the mistakes and how to rectify them.
parts.answer: Thaabitatan ثابتة should be thaabitan ثابتا, as it is the haal and it should correlate in N&G to the zul haal (pronoun هو inside يثبت).
parts.doubt: The sentence field spells the verb as يَنبُثُ (yanbuthu), root ن ب ث, meaning to spread or emanate. But the teacher's explanation talks about the pronoun inside يثبت (yathbutu), root ث ب ت, the same root as ثابتة. These are two different Arabic words, not just missing vowel marks. Either the sentence text has a typo, or the explanation names the wrong verb. Worth checking against the source picture haal-23.png.

parts.doubt: The sentence field spells the disputed word as ثلاثةُ, with a dammah. But part a's question quotes the same word as ثلاثةَ, with a fathah. Part c says the mistake is exactly this ending, it should be a fathah because the word is a zarf. So part a's question already shows the corrected spelling, not the mistake being tested. The question text does not match the sentence field.

parts.question: How many mistakes?
Explain the mistakes and how to rectify them.
parts.answer: The word ثلاثة should have a fathah as it is zarf (time/place). The مضاف إليه of إكرام should be plural, هم, as it is referring to the guests who are plural.

parts.question:
Is this sentence written correctly: "أكل زيدٌ هو شبعانِ ثُمَّ تَأَلَّمَ بَطنُها
Zaid ate whilst he was satiated then his stomach ached."?
How many mistakes?
Explain the mistakes and how to rectify them.
parts.answer: There should be a waaw haaliyyah before 'هو' because the haal 'هو شبعان' is a jumlah ismiyyah which begins with the dhameer raabit. Also, شبعانِ should be شبعانُ as it is مرفوع because of being the خبر of هو and it's also غير منصرف hence no tanween. Also, it should be 'بطنه' because it is referring to the stomach of zaid and he is male (hopefully).

examples.sentence:

Zaid ate whilst he was satiated then his stomach ached.
